notes: Dey et al. (2015), Section 3.2.2, p. 7, quote 0.46 kJ/kg.K for sponge iron (citing Hajidavalloo and Alagheband). That matches iron's room-temperature heat capacity; a mean value from 25 to 1020 degC has to include the alpha-gamma transition and is higher, so 0.46 is not adopted for a hot-discharge sensible heat. Closing this needs a NIST enthalpy weighting over the DRI phases.

Open: Dey (2015) gives no char or ash heat capacity, and the web search found only an abstract (Fuel, 'The specific heats of coals, cokes and their ashes') measuring cokes to 600 K and ashes to 1000 K, not a mean to 1020 degC for a char-ash mix. Affects the char, free-ash and dust sensible-heat lines only.
